tip: 가랑비에 옷 젖다 (garangbie ot jeotda = drizzle soaks clothes) = small things pile up unnoticed.
시작이 반이다 (sijagi banida = the start is half) = getting started is the hardest part.
사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 간다 (sagongi maneumyeon baega saneuro ganda) = too many cooks spoil the broth.
벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다 (byeoneun igeulsurok gogaereul suginda) = the wiser one grows, the humbler.
김칫국부터 마신다 (gimchitgukbuteo masinda = drinking the broth first) = counting chickens before they hatch.
가는 날이 장날 (ganeun nari jangnal = the day you go is market day) = an unlucky coincidence.
언 발에 오줌 누기 (eon bare ojum nugi = peeing on frozen feet) = a stopgap that soon backfires.
가뭄에 콩 나듯 (gamume kong nadeut = like beans in a drought) = very rare, few and far between.
새옹지마 (saeongjima) is 'the frontier old man's horse': it ran off (bad), came back with another (good), his son fell off it (bad). Fortune keeps flipping – the whole saying in four syllables.
유비무환 (yubimuhwan, 有備無患) = with preparation, there is no worry.
일석이조 (ilseogijo, 一石二鳥) = one stone, two birds.
금상첨화 (geumsangcheomhwa, 錦上添花) = flowers added to brocade; a welcome bonus.
설상가상 (seolsanggasang, 雪上加霜) = frost on top of snow; troubles pile up.
대기만성 (daegimanseong, 大器晩成) = a great talent matures slowly.
사면초가 (samyeonchoga, 四面楚歌) = surrounded on all sides with no way out.
반신반의 (bansinbanui, 半信半疑) = half-believing, half-doubting.
천고마비 (cheongomabi) is literally 'sky high, horses fat' – autumn air is clear and the harvest fattens the horses. Four syllables that mean the perfect crisp season.
발이 넓다 (bari neolda = feet are wide) = to be well-connected.
눈이 높다 (nuni nopda = eyes are high) = to have high standards.
손이 크다 (soni keuda = hands are big) = to be generous and lavish.
입이 무겁다 (ibi mugeopda = mouth is heavy) = discreet, keeps secrets.
귀가 얇다 (gwiga yalda = ears are thin) = easily persuaded.
미역국을 먹다 (miyeokgugeul meokda = to eat seaweed soup) = to fail an exam or interview.
국수를 먹이다 (guksureul meogida = to feed someone noodles) = to get married; the wedding guests are the ones served noodles.
발등에 불이 떨어지다 (baldeunge buri tteoreojida = fire lands on your feet) = a sudden, pressing crisis.
파김치가 되다 (pagimchiga doeda = to become limp scallion kimchi) = to be worn out.
새 발의 피 (sae barui pi = blood on a bird's foot) = a trivial, tiny amount.
간이 크다 (gani keuda = liver is big) = bold, daring.
어깨가 무겁다 (eokkaega mugeopda = shoulders are heavy) = to feel burdened by responsibility.
입이 짧다 (ibi jjalda = mouth is short) = to be a picky eater.
